records.gloss: For the director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
pieces: For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 3, the title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
alternatives: for the end (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word (menatseach) is a form of a verb meaning to lead or oversee; 1 Chronicles 15:21 uses the verb for Levites who led the singing with lyres. It stands at the head of 55 psalms, probably marking the psalm for the leader of the temple music. The ancient Greek translation read it differently, as "for the end".

decisions.choice: stringed instruments: to be accompanied on strings
decisions.reason: The word (neginot) is used for music played on strings (Habakkuk 3:19 ends with the same note). It tells how the psalm was to be performed.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

records.heading: Lying down in peace

records.source: בְּקָרְאִ֡י עֲנֵ֤נִי׀אֱלֹ֘הֵ֤י צִדְקִ֗י בַּ֭צָּר הִרְחַ֣בְתָּ לִּ֑י חָ֝נֵּ֗נִי וּשְׁמַ֥ע תְּפִלָּתִֽי׃
records.gloss: When I call, answer me, God of my righteousness! In the distress you made room for me; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
pieces: When I call, answer me, God who stands up for my right! When I was hemmed in, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave me room. Show me grace now and listen to my prayer.

L.2: When I call, answer me, God of my righteousness! In [the] distress {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made room for me; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.

R.2: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who shows that I am in the right. Please answer when I call to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! When I was in trouble, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set me free. Be kind to me now and hear my prayer.

decisions.choice: God of my righteousness: the God who upholds my right
decisions.reason: Righteousness (tsedeq) here is being in the right, as in a court. The psalmist is falsely accused (verse 3) and appeals to the God who will show that he is in the right. The phrase may also mean simply "my righteous God".

decisions.choice: in distress you made room for me: set me free from a tight place
decisions.reason: Distress (tsar) is a narrow, tight place; to make room (rachab) is to make it wide. Being rescued is pictured as being brought out into open space (Psalm 18:20).

decisions.choice: you have made room: what God has done before
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past form between two requests. It most likely recalls an earlier rescue, the ground for asking again; some read it as a request.

decisions.choice: God who stands up for my right (B); the one who shows that I am in the right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means here (m1); Literal keeps its form.

records.source: בְּנֵ֥י אִ֡ישׁ עַד־מֶ֬ה כְבוֹדִ֣י לִ֭כְלִמָּה תֶּאֱהָב֣וּן רִ֑יק תְּבַקְשׁ֖וּ כָזָ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Sons of man, until when [will] my honor [be] for shame? [Will] you love emptiness, seek falsehood? Selah.
pieces: You people, how long will my honor be dragged into disgrace? How long will you love empty things and go looking for lies? Selah

L.3: Sons of man, how long [will] my glory [be turned] into shame? [How long] will you love emptiness [and] seek falsehood? Selah

R.3: You people, how long will you insult me and bring me shame? How long will you love worthless things and go after lies? Selah

decisions.choice: sons of man: you people, perhaps men of standing
decisions.reason: The phrase (bene 'ish) is addressed to the psalmist's opponents. Psalm 49:3 sets it beside another phrase for people in a way that may mean "high and low", so these may be men of rank who are attacking his honor.

decisions.choice: my glory: my honor, my good name
decisions.reason: The word (kavod) is the one used in 3:4, "my glory": a person's weight and standing. His opponents are trying to shame him.

decisions.choice: emptiness, falsehood: worthless things and lies
decisions.reason: Emptiness (riq) is the word of 2:1, plans with nothing in them; falsehood (kazav) is a lie. They may be the slanders against the psalmist, or, as "lies" means in Amos 2:4, false gods.

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: Balanced says "honor" because the sense here is reputation (m2); Literal keeps "glory", as in 3:4.

decisions.choice: how long will you insult me and bring me shame
alternatives: how long will my glory be turned into shame
decisions.reason: Readable makes the opponents the subject, which the question implies.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: וּדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־הִפְלָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה חָסִ֣יד ל֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע בְּקָרְאִ֥י אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And know that YHWH has set apart [the] faithful [one] for himself; YHWH hears when I call to him.
pieces: Be sure of this: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set apart the one who is faithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hear me when I call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.4: And know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has set apart [the] faithful one for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hears when I call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.4: Know this: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen the person who is loyal to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hears me when I call to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: set apart: made distinct, marked out
decisions.reason: The verb (palah) is used for the LORD making a distinction between Israel and Egypt (Exodus 9:4; 11:7). The faithful person belongs to the LORD and is treated differently.

decisions.choice: the faithful one: one who is loyal to God
decisions.reason: The word (chasid) comes from the word for steadfast, loyal love (chesed). It is the person who keeps faith with God. The psalmist means himself, but what he says is true of anyone who is faithful.

decisions.choice: faithful to him (B); loyal to him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say to whom the person is faithful (m2).

records.source: רִגְז֗וּ וְֽאַל־תֶּ֫חֱטָ֥אוּ אִמְר֣וּ בִ֭לְבַבְכֶם עַֽל־מִשְׁכַּבְכֶ֗ם וְדֹ֣מּוּ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Tremble, and do not sin; speak in your heart on your bed, and be still. Selah.
pieces: Tremble, and do not sin. Lying on your bed, reason it out in your own heart, and be still. Selah

L.5: Tremble, and do not sin; speak in your heart on your bed, and be silent. Selah

R.5: Shake with fear, and stop sinning. When you lie down at night, think hard about this and be quiet. Selah

decisions.choice: tremble: shake with fear
decisions.reason: The verb (ragaz) means to shake or be stirred, with fear or with anger. Here the opponents are told to stand in awe of the LORD and stop. The ancient Greek translation has "be angry, and do not sin", the words Paul quotes in Ephesians 4:26.

decisions.choice: speak in your heart: think it over
decisions.reason: To speak in one's heart is to think, to reason with oneself (Genesis 17:17). The night, alone on one's bed, is the time for it.

decisions.choice: be silent: be still, stop
decisions.reason: The verb (damam) means to be silent or still: the opponents should end their accusations.

decisions.choice: Shake with fear
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of trembling is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: Sacrifice sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in YHWH.
pieces: Bring sacrifices as they should be brought, and rely on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: Sacrifice sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: Bring your offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the right way, and trust in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: sacrifices of righteousness: sacrifices offered rightly
decisions.reason: The phrase (zivche tsedeq) is used in Deuteronomy 33:19 and Psalm 51:21: sacrifices offered in the right way, by people who are right with God. A sacrifice without trust in the LORD is not what he asks.

decisions.choice: Sacrifice ... trust: still spoken to the opponents
decisions.reason: The commands continue those of verse 5: the people who shamed the psalmist are told to turn to the LORD.

decisions.choice: Bring sacrifices as they should be brought
decisions.reason: Balanced says what makes the sacrifices right (m1).

records.source: רַבִּ֥ים אֹמְרִים֮ מִֽי־יַרְאֵ֪נ֫וּט֥וֹב נְֽסָה־עָ֭לֵינוּ א֨וֹר פָּנֶ֬יךָ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Many [are] saying, Who will show us good? Lift up on us the light of your face, YHWH.
pieces: Many are saying, "Who will let us see good times?" {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} shining face toward us.

L.7: Many [are] saying, "Who will show us good?" Lift up on us the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: Many people ask, "Who will give us good things?" {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, smile on us and be kind to us.

decisions.choice: good: good times, a good harvest
decisions.reason: Good (tov) here is prosperity, the rain and harvest that verse 8 goes on to speak of.

decisions.choice: Lift up ...: the psalmist's prayer
alternatives: the rest of what the many say
decisions.reason: The question is what many are saying; the second line may continue their words or be the psalmist's answer. Since he goes on in verse 8 to speak to the LORD, the line is read as his prayer.

decisions.choice: the light of your face: the priestly blessing
decisions.reason: The words echo the blessing of Numbers 6:25-26: "the LORD make his face shine on you ... the LORD lift up his face on you". A shining face is God's favor.

decisions.choice: turn your shining face toward us (B); smile on us and be kind to us (R)
alternatives: lift up the light of your face on us
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the shining face; Readable says what it means (m3).

records.source: נָתַ֣תָּה שִׂמְחָ֣ה בְלִבִּ֑י מֵעֵ֬ת דְּגָנָ֖ם וְתִֽירוֹשָׁ֣ם רָֽבּוּ׃
records.gloss: You have put joy in my heart, more than [at the] time their grain and their new wine abound.
pieces: The joy {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have put in my heart is greater than theirs at harvest, when grain and new wine overflow.

L.8: You have put joy in my heart, more than [at the] time [when] their grain and their new wine abound.

R.8: You have made me happier than people are at harvest time, when they have plenty of grain and wine.

decisions.choice: grain and new wine: a rich harvest
decisions.reason: Grain and new wine (tirosh, the freshly pressed juice) are the harvest that God's blessing brings (Deuteronomy 7:13). "Their" is the many of verse 7, who look for good things.

decisions.choice: more than at the time: joy greater than theirs
decisions.reason: The joy God gives the psalmist is greater than the joy others have when the harvest is good.

decisions.choice: greater than theirs at harvest
alternatives: more than when their grain and new wine abound
decisions.reason: Balanced names the time the grain and wine come in (m1).

records.source: בְּשָׁל֣וֹם יַחְדָּו֮ אֶשְׁכְּבָ֪ה וְאִ֫ישָׁ֥ן כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה לְבָדָ֑ד לָ֝בֶ֗טַח תּוֹשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: In peace together I will lie down and sleep, for you, YHWH, alone, in safety make me dwell.
pieces: I will lie down in peace and fall asleep at once, because it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone, who let me live in safety.

L.9: In peace together I will lie down and sleep, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, alone, in safety make me dwell.

R.9: When I lie down, I will go to sleep right away, feeling at peace, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, are the only one who keeps me safe.

decisions.choice: together: at once, both
decisions.reason: The word (yachdav) joins lying down and sleeping: he lies down and sleeps at once, without lying awake in fear (compare 3:6).

decisions.choice: alone: you alone
alternatives: though I am alone, you make me dwell in safety
decisions.reason: The word (levadad) most likely goes with "you": the LORD and no one else keeps him safe. It may instead describe the psalmist, safe though alone, as Israel "dwells in safety, alone" in Deuteronomy 33:28.

decisions.choice: peace: wholeness and safety
decisions.reason: Peace (shalom) is more than calm: it is well-being and safety, which the last line names.

decisions.choice: fall asleep at once (B); go to sleep right away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "together" means here (m1).
